data.error: category must be one of: dhcp, dns, hardware, monitoring, routing, service, wan

data.reason: The firewall's WAN interface driver (vtnet0) has a hung transmit queue — repeated "watchdog timeout on queue 0" with ~48k output errors — so no packets leave the firewall even though the interface is up, holds its lease (198.51.100.27), and the cable modem is registered/OPERATIONAL; the WAN watchdog's interface reloads cannot clear the stuck queue.

data.cause: The firewall's WAN interface driver (vtnet0) has a hung transmit queue — repeated "watchdog timeout on queue 0" with ~48k output errors — so no packets leave the firewall even though the interface is up, holds its lease (198.51.100.27), and the cable modem is registered/OPERATIONAL; the WAN watchdog's interface reloads cannot clear the stuck queue.
evidence: dmesg -a shows repeated 'vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0' alternating with 'vtnet0: link state changed to DOWN/UP' — the TX queue repeatedly stalls while the link itself keeps coming back.
netstat -i: vtnet0 Opkts=60211873 with Oerrs=48211 (large accumulated transmit errors), while vtnet1 (LAN) shows 0 errors — problem is isolated to the WAN NIC.
ping -c 3 198.51.100.1 and ping -c 3 1.1.1.1 both fail with 'ping: sendto: No buffer space available' (ENOBUFS) — the output path to the ISP next hop is stuck, not merely filtered.
arp -a -n: gateway entry '(198.51.100.1) at (incomplete)' — even ARP resolution of the ISP next hop fails because probes cannot egress, consistent with a hung TX queue.

ifconfig vtnet0: flags UP,RUNNING,LOWER_UP, status active, inet 198.51.100.27 — physical link and addressing are fine, so this is neither wan_link nor a lost DHCP lease; netstat -rn shows a valid default via 198.51.100.1.

/var/db/wan-watchdog/state.json + events.jsonl: outage since ~02:01, 4 WAN reloads during this outage all rc=0 with no recovery, and at 03:30 the watchdog hit its cap (reloads_24h=12/12) — repeated interface reloads do not clear the hang.

modem-metrics.jsonl / modem-events.jsonl: after an initial 'No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out' (02:01:44) and a modem self-reboot, the modem reports OPERATIONAL with good SNR (37.6-37.8 dB) since 02:29 — the provider side recovered, but the firewall still can't send, so the remaining fault is local to the WAN NIC/driver.
data.recommendation: Reboot the firewall (gw.lan) to reset the hung vtnet0 transmit queue — that is the only way to reinitialize the NIC given that repeated wan_reload cycles already failed (4 in this outage, 12 in 24h). The maintainer is away tonight, so let the harness apply firewall_reboot under its fallback rules; expect ~4 minutes of network outage. A wan_reload alone would not help: it renewed the lease fine every time while the driver stayed stuck. After recovery, consider replacing or updating the virtio NIC/driver if watchdog timeouts recur.
